title: Customs Tariff Amendment (Incorporation of Proposals and Other Measures) Bill 2020
short_title: Customs Tariff Amendment (Incorporation of Proposals and Other Measures) Bill 2020

divisions.question: The majority voted in favour of a [motion](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/debate/?id=2021-02-17.14.4) to keep the usual second reading motion unchanged. In parliamentary jargon, they voted "*that the words proposed to be omitted stand part of the question.*" The usual second reading motion is "*that the bill be read a [second time](https://peo.gov.au/understand-our-parliament/how-parliament-works/bills-and-laws/making-a-law-in-the-australian-parliament/),*" which is parliamentary jargon for agreeing with the main idea of the bill. This vote took place after Gorton MP [Brendan O'Connor](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/representatives/gorton/brendan_o'connor) (Labor) proposed the amendment below. ### Proposed amendment text > *That all words after "That" be omitted with a view to substituting the following words:* > > *"whilst not declining to give the bill a second reading, the House:* > > *(1) acknowledges the bill provides for reduced rates of customs duty for goods required to combat the COVID-19 pandemic; and* > > *(2) notes that the Government has failed to outline a plan to address the economic impacts of COVID-19."*

speeches.speaker: Jason Wood
speeches.brief: The bill incorporates temporary concessional customs duty rates for COVID-19 medical supplies (face masks, soaps, eyewear) from February to December 2020, and makes six further amendments: new tariff subheadings for formulated caffeinated beverages, supplementary foods and sports foods; realignments for wheelie bins, vitamin/medicament classification and metal parts; removal of the $12,000 special customs duty on used vehicles from Peru and the Trans-Pacific Partnership; and deletion of redundant phasing rates from free trade agreements.

speeches.speaker: Brendan O'Connor
speeches.brief: The speaker moved an amendment supporting the bill’s reduced customs duty for COVID-19 medical products but argued the government has failed to outline a plan to address the economic impacts, noting over 200,000 jobs lost and nearly 2.1 million Australians unemployed or underemployed.

speeches.speaker: Jason Wood
speeches.brief: The Customs Tariff Amendment (Incorporation of Proposals and Other Measures) Bill 2020 incorporates tariff proposals providing temporary concessions for COVID-19 medical supplies like face masks and soaps, creates new tariff classifications for certain goods, removes the $12,000 special duty on used motor vehicles from two free trade agreements, and deletes redundant provisions.
